name: Postgres transaction helper
purpose: The helper that wraps the transaction-control primitives around a consumer callback and rolls back with a transactionRolledBack event on any error, tracking the zero-based index of the failing statement inside the callback. The transaction-control shape is owned on `interfaces.withTransaction` below.
responsibilities: Acquire a pg.PoolClient from the facade's pool; open the transaction through the BEGIN primitive owned on interfaces.withTransaction (AC-27104-1).
Invoke the consumer callback with a wrapped client whose query(sql, params) delegates to the underlying client and increments a statement counter each time it is called (AC-27104-1).
On the callback's successful completion, close the transaction through the COMMIT primitive owned on interfaces.withTransaction, release the client, resolve the outer promise (AC-27104-1).

On any error thrown from a wrapped-client query or from the callback body, unwind the transaction through the ROLLBACK primitive owned on interfaces.withTransaction, fire transactionRolledBack on the injected event sink with { statementIndex, code }, release the client, re-throw the underlying error (AC-27104-1).
Preserve the underlying pg error object (code, detail, position, table, constraint) on the re-thrown error so the facade's own error boundary constructs the internal error record correctly.
internalStructure: A single async function withTransaction({ pool, onEvent }) that returns a call helper. The helper wraps the pg.PoolClient in a proxy that intercepts .query() to increment the counter, forwards the arguments to the underlying client, and re-throws on error after firing the event.

interfaces.name: withTransaction
interfaces.description: await store.withTransaction(async (tx) => { await tx.query(...); await tx.query(...); }). The helper acquires a pg.PoolClient from the pool and issues the transaction-control primitives around the callback: `client.query('BEGIN')` before the first wrapped-client query, `client.query('COMMIT')` on the callback's successful return, and `client.query('ROLLBACK')` on any thrown error before releasing the client. On rollback the helper fires transactionRolledBack on the injected event sink with { statementIndex, code } and re-throws the underlying pg error.

dependencies.name: Postgres facade
dependencies.description: The facade owns the pool the helper acquires from and the event sink the rollback event fires on.

tradeoffs: Wrapping the client in a proxy adds one function-call hop per query; on a hot path this is negligible. Tracking statementIndex by counting calls does not survive nested withTransaction invocations (Postgres does not support nested transactions natively; savepoints would be a v1.1 minor). Consumers that need savepoints today drop to raw client.query('SAVEPOINT ...') inside the callback and accept that statementIndex points at the outer BEGIN sequence.
